startup.name: Visibl Semiconductors
startup.description: An AI native custom silicon design partner that cuts ASIC cost and timeline on mature nodes for power electronics makers, handling architecture, verification, fabrication and packaging so hardware teams need no chip team. Team of 3 in San Francisco, Winter 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts on the as of date, so this is a note only. A random applicant starts near 1 percent (yc_acceptance.md, 0.6 to 2 percent range). Hard tech with a clear customer pain and AI timing fits YC interest, but a three person team promising a full chip path is ambitious and no customer is named.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because chip design takes years and millions of dollars, and three people cannot show a design win at application time. A design partner model also looks like consulting. Reviewers would ask why AI tools make mature node ASICs cheaper than established design houses, and for a named customer.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window of 10.4 months to 2026-11-17 and a round above about $1M. The ever anchor is about 0.65 and about 60 percent of raisers close inside 10 months. AI plus chips and power for data centers draws investor interest, but a 3 person team needs capital for tape outs, so the plan is held at the anchor and no lift is applied. The odds do not rank Visibl against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels or a small fund on top of the YC deal. Common for design services revenue funding early engagements.
Typical institutional seed, near the 2022+ median of 4.1M. Typical seed for a hard tech company with an anchor customer.
Upside seed led by a top fund. Chip and power infrastructure investors fund larger seeds when a named customer commits to a tape out.
Large seed, only with a landmark traction story or a hot thesis. Needs a funded customer program and a marquee lead.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed fails if the company has design services pilots but no customer committed to a multi million dollar tape out, since chip investors want a path to product revenue. Three people cannot staff several chip projects, and foundry runs need capital. Analogs Tensil and Vathys never got beyond the YC check, and Reduced Energy Microsystems raised only a $2M seed before going inactive.

ladder.why_it_fails: The company stops before a Series C if it stays a design services firm with margins capped by engineer hours, or if power chip incumbents such as Texas Instruments and Infineon cut prices on standard parts. A sale to an incumbent that wants design talent is the likelier exit than a growth round.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Failure comes from services economics, slow tape outs and customers choosing off the shelf parts. Chip analogs such as Tensil and Vathys never passed the YC check, and Reduced Energy Microsystems stopped after a $2M seed. A decent outcome is an acquisition by a power semiconductor company that wants the design flow and team.

killers.mitigation: Charge royalties or unit pricing on volume.

killers.mitigation: Target volume products where board cost matters.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing, verifying, fabricating and packaging silicon is among the hardest work for a small team, with expensive mistakes and long cycles. Mature nodes and BCD processes lower cost, and AI tools help design and verification, but a team of 3 still depends on foundry access, IP and test capacity.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbent EDA vendors and design houses could add AI flows, but custom power design for small volume customers is not their focus, and the cycle time is long.

evidence.claim: Power management ICs are cited as a bottleneck for data centers, with lead times of 20 to 40 weeks and tight mature node capacity.
Design services firms sell custom PMIC design, which shows customers pay for it.

roadmap.proof: Silicon passing customer qualification and a volume order.

brand.rationale: The name is descriptive and the Semiconductors word helps hardware buyers place it, similar to plain industry names in hard tech. The spelling and length are weak for word of mouth, but chip buyers decide on technical proof.

narrative.headline: A technically ambitious chip design partner where a seed above $1M inside 10 months is plausible but unproven, and later rounds depend on silicon.
narrative.general_summary: Visibl offers AI assisted custom silicon design for power electronics makers on mature nodes. The pain is real, since power chip lead times were long and standard parts limit cost, and chip and power infrastructure were attractive to investors. The risks are heavy: a three person team, long tape out cycles, a services like model and incumbent suppliers. A seed above $1M within the 10.4 month window is plausible near the B2B cohort pace if a customer commits to a program, and a Series A inside the window is rare because silicon takes more than a year. These odds do not rank Visibl against others. A good path is a customer funded program that supports a seed of $3M to $6M.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05 from the input file and market searches only.
Window is 10.4 months to 2026-11-17; seed means a round above about $1M.
The Semiconductors tag has no researched calibration companies, so B2B and Hard Tech cohorts are used and treated as anecdotes.
